title: The Microscope I Brought from Cairo
film_language: English; onscreen first-person text, no synthetic narrator
archival_post: 1 July 2017 (post date, not verified camera date)
design: An archival photograph explored as a quiet two-minute visual essay. Unmodified original shown at opening and closing. Detail crops are editorial, not new evidentiary photographs.
methodological_note: Personal recollection documents the purchase and transport. The photographs show the microscope at home in Qatar, not the purchase, travel, or scientific measurements.

scenes.title: An ordinary morning
scenes.text: This is my microscope at home in Qatar. The photograph was posted on 1 July 2017; the original camera date is not verified.

scenes.title: Qasr El Einy → Qatar
scenes.text: I bought the instrument in the Qasr El Einy area of Cairo. Getting it to Qatar took considerable effort. This journey is remembered, not photographed.
scenes.note: First-person recollection · typographic representation, not travel footage

scenes.title: A microscope of my own
scenes.text: I wanted to be able to return to an observation when the question occurred to me, not only during scheduled laboratory hours.

scenes.title: Inside the scheduled laboratory
scenes.text: University instruments came with protocols and calendars, for good reasons. I valued that training, but curiosity kept its own hours.
scenes.note: Separate laboratory internship photograph · contextual only

scenes.title: No assigned experiment
scenes.text: The photograph shows a vacation morning: books, notes and an American Chemical Society mug. No supervisor was waiting for a result.
scenes.note: Original personal photograph · editorial detail composition

scenes.title: The freedom to return
scenes.text: At home, I could come back to the same object another day. I could spend time looking, change my mind, and look again.

scenes.title: Seeing is not knowing
scenes.text: A microscope lets you see. Explanation still needs controls, methods and evidence that other people can examine. I had a place to practice the first part.

scenes.title: Among ordinary things
scenes.text: It stood there on my desk, among the ordinary objects of a morning at home. Scientific attention had somewhere to live between classes.
scenes.note: Personal microscope photograph · full source retained

scenes.title: The microscope from Cairo
scenes.text: The instrument came from Cairo. The photograph is from Qatar. What I remember most is having the time to ask questions that belonged to me.
scenes.note: Original personal photograph · no experiment claimed
